text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- CGIP buys a 20.2 percent stake in Valeo from Carlo de Benedetti's Cerus for 330 francs a share. JP Morgan and state bank CDC also buy small stakes. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
LES ECHOS
-- Airbus Industries gets order for 16 aircraft from Emirates Airlines.
-- Government postpones plans to reform SNCF state-owned railway operator.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- Employers' federation sceptical about expected economic pickup for 1997, calls forecast growth of two percent unsatisfactory.
-- Schlumberger to buy microchip card maker Solaic, a Sligos subsidiary, while businessman Marc Lassus strengthens control over Gemplus.
-- Thomson Multimedia agrees with Oracle to start selling terminals in 1997 allowing customers to connect to the Internet via their television set.
-- New car registrations were up 24 percent in October, in the wake of a government incentive scheme for buyers of new cars that expired in September.
L'AGEFI
-- EU audit committee does not oppose France's plan to use a 37.5 billion franc payment from France Telecom to help meet 1997 budget goals and qualify for a single European currency.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Markets expect an alliance between insurers AXA and UAP despite denials by both companies. Shares in UAP rose 2.9 percent yesterday.
-- Managing director of state-controlled nuclear plant builder Framatome criticises plans for a merger with GEC-Alsthom as "a very bad idea".
-- Airbus and Rolls-Royce reach preliminary agreement on engine cooperation for future large carrier.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- CGT union calls for mid-November strikes to pressure the government to call off austerity measures.
-- Merrill Lynch executive says company considers making a bid for French bank Pallas-Stern, which went into receivership this year due to indebtedness.
